reason: The current LightGCN scores items only through history-aware dot products; a separate item intercept could capture marginal selection frequency without overloading embeddings. Its macro validation HR@10 of 0.5575 and Electronics score of 0.365 motivate this controlled experiment but do not establish popularity calibration as the cause. Historical results support retaining target-excluded profiles, while the weaker sampled-softmax and recency-weighting experiments argue against combining this bias addition with further objective changes. Modify model_design for scoring and training_evaluation for optimization, export, and predictor consistency.

plan.model_design: Add LightGCN.item_bias as a zero-initialized trainable vector of length itemnum + 1, keeping padding bias zero and adding item_bias[p] to positive_scores and item_bias[n] to negative_scores before the existing temperature-1 sampled-softmax cross-entropy. This isolates the hypothesis that explicit item intercepts improve ranking against uniform candidates; preserve uniform loss averaging rather than reintroducing the historically unsuccessful recency-weighted reduction. Extend PredictionModel.__init__(user_ids, user_vectors, item_vectors) with an optional trailing item_bias=None argument, register the supplied bias as a buffer with a zero-vector default, and add self.item_bias[candidates] to its existing dot-product scores without changing PredictionModel.forward(user_ids, histories, history_mask, candidates). Preserve existing variable names, LightGCN constructor arguments, training_vectors() return signature, target_excluded_vectors(), and export(original_user_ids), while making export carry a detached cloned bias alongside embeddings. Keep two propagation layers, DIM=64, complete histories, half-life 10, profile coefficient 0.5, and differentiable target exclusion across repeated positives unchanged.
plan.training_evaluation: In train_dataset(ds, device, deadline), retain optimizer construction over model.parameters() so Adam learns item_bias at learning rate 0.003, and extend regularizer with (model.item_bias[p].square().sum() + model.item_bias[n].square().mean(dim=1).sum()) / (2.0 * BATCH), retaining loss = ranking + 1e-4 * regularizer and the existing embedding terms. Update checkpoint reconstruction and write_predict_script() to pass state['item_bias'] into PredictionModel, preserving train_dataset(), write_predict_script(), predict(user_id, history, candidates, *, dataset_name=None), dataset routing, and existing variable names so internal validation and host inference use identical biased scoring. Extend the existing deterministic fixtures to verify zero-bias equivalence, candidate-wise nonzero bias additions, finite bias gradients, and checkpoint/generated-predictor parity without advancing training RNG state; retain existing target-exclusion checks. Explicitly keep preprocessing seed 0, training/evaluation seed 42, supplied splits, all four categories, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, 32 uniform unseen negatives, BATCH=8192, STEPS=8, SASREC_EPOCHS default 200, clipping, deadlines, checkpoint selection, and early stopping unchanged. Assess the hypothesis using the unchanged pinned host validation protocol of 200 users per category and 99 unique negatives, comparing equal-weight macro HR@10 against 0.5575 and category scores against 0.575/0.595/0.365/0.695, without hidden-test access, additional data, pretrained weights, evaluator changes, or claims of measured improvement.
